To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have purified form A DNA-dependent RNA polymerase from rat liver nucleoli using mild low- ionic-strength extraction procedures.

we have developed a procedure for the purification of forms AI and AII RNA polymerase from rat liver using low-ionic strength conditions and have shown that these enzymes are similar in properties to the Escherichia coil enzyme.
we have purified form AI and form AII RNA polymerases to apparent homogeneity from rat-liver nuclei using a low-ionic-strenght extraction procedure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of form AI and form AII enzymes, which are responsible for the synthesis of ribosomal RNA.
the isolation of the various forms of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase from rat liver.
the isolation and characterization of form A RNA-dependent polymerases from mammalian cells, and with the elucidation of the role of these enzymes in the transcription of the genes for ribosomal RNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

forms AI and AII represent two different enzymes which are responsible for the synthesis of ribosomal RNA in the nucleolus, and form B represents a single enzyme responsible for the synthesis in the nucleoplasm of RNA of a different size to that of ribosomal RNA, and which is distinct from the enzymes of forms AI and Aii.
forms AI and AII RNA polymerase are present in nucleoli and form B in the nucleoplasm.
the method described here has been successful in purifying form A RNA polymerases from nucleoli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have purified two form A enzymes from rat liver nucleoli and one form B enzyme from rat liver nucleoplasm, which are free of DNases and RNases and have a similar size and properties to those from E. coli.
form AI and A II enzymes have been purified in a form that is free of contaminating activities.

the form A enzymes are present as two distinct enzymes in rat liver nucleoli, that they can be separated from each other and from the other forms of RNA polymerase by ion-exchange chromatographic procedures, and that the form AI enzyme is the enzyme which transcribes the ribosomal RNA genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
form A RNA polymerases from nucleoli can be purified under low-ionic-strenght conditions.
the use of low ionic strength conditions is essential for the purification of forms AI and AII.
it is possible to isolate form AI and A II enzymes from rat liver nucleoli under mild conditions.
